title: room-policy §5 spells parent_dependant two ways, and the prose spelling is not the wire field
description:
Found 2026-11-23 while writing the parent-dependent conditions into
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 §Room/create (bead mimid-1wgh.114.4).

THE INCONSISTENCY, in draft-ietf-mimi-room-policy-04:
- prose, txt L532: "In rooms with parent_dependent set to true (a
  parent-dependent room)";
- prose, txt L542: "A room can be both fixed_membership and
  parent_dependent";
- the TLS presentation language, txt L572 and L3678: "bool
  parent_dependant;".

So the field is named one way in the struct and another in every prose
mention of it. "dependent" is the correct English adjective, which is
presumably why the prose has it, but the struct is what is normative for
the wire.

WHY IT IS NOT ONLY COSMETIC: an implementer who writes a schema, a code
generator, or a test fixture from the prose gets a field name that does
not exist, and one who greps the document for the struct's name misses
every sentence that explains what the field means. mimid hit the second
half: our code uses parent_dependant, with comments noting the spelling,
and our own prose in beads and docs drifts to parent_dependent.

PROPOSED: one spelling throughout. Changing the struct to
parent_dependent is the better English and the breaking change; changing
the prose to parent_dependant keeps the wire stable and looks like a typo
forever. Either is better than both. The WG should pick, and -04 is
pre-adoption enough that the struct could still move.

WHAT WE DID MEANWHILE: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 §Room/create
conditions 8 and 9 use the STRUCT spelling, parent_dependant, because
that is the field an implementation reads, even though it disagrees with
room-policy's own prose. If the WG settles on the other spelling, that
text follows.

Low priority: it costs nobody correctness today, only grep. Filing it so
it is not rediscovered a third time.
